title: Sekiro Side Story: Hanbei the Undying Chapter 1

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Hanbei the Undying
Shinazu Hanbee
Sekiro Side Story: Hanbei the Undying

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text:
On a battlefield during the Sengoku period, Sword Saint Isshin Ashina kill the enemy general, Tamura. A warrior then approaches Isshin. Isshin wonders if he intends to avenge his lord, but tells him that the war is now over and he should kill himself, however the warrior states that he will seek vengeance as long as he lives. The two prepare to fight. Isshin strikes with Ashina Sword Style Ichimonji, but the warrior manages to deflect it. Isshin is impressed, but then immediately strikes with Ichimonji Double, slicing through the warrior's sword and cutting him in half. Later as the crows feed on the corpses, the dead warrior awakens.
About twenty years later, in the north, the Land of Ashina, Isshin had created his own clan, the Ashina Clan. However Isshin is not immortal and won't live forever. The internal minister backed by central political power of Japan, is plotting to subjugate Isshin's land in the name of unifying the country.
Wandering around, Hanbei approaches a village nested between the mountains of Ashina. Seeing the stranger, Shoukichi, a young man stops him, telling him that he cannot pass. Seeing that his hands shake while holding the sword, Hanbei ignores him and proceeds. Annoyed for being ignored, Shoukichi strikes, but Hanbei raises his hand to protect himself. However the strike isn't strong enough and is unable to cut Hanbei's bone. Shoukichi gets scared, but in that moment Hanbei collapses. Shoukichi's sister, Suzu, then shows up and Shoukichi brags that he killed the man. Suzu is worried that he may have killed a guest of Takamine of Ashina, but Shoukichi doubts it as he looks like a disgraced warrior. Suzu then notices that Hanbei is still alive and brings him to their house.
When Hanbei awakens, Suzu apologizes, explaining that everyone in the village is on edge, as they expect the internal minister forces to attack any moment. Suzu then offers some food, but explains that they don't have much. A man then comes knocking at their door and informs Shoukichi that the men who went into the mountains got ambushed, and now a group of brigands is heading towards the village. Shoukichi then heads out, but tells Hanbei to leave after he eats. He feels fine leaving him since Hanbei looks half-dead and won't be able to swing a sword with the wound he gave him.
Shoukichi and his friend, feel confident since they have Yatomaru at their side, who learned the Ashina sword style at Takamine's dojo. However as they face the brigands, Yatomaru gets killed. Shoukichi is the only one standing from the villagers, but he refuses to give up. As the brigands prepare to kill him, Shoukichi sees Hanbei approaching.
A bit earlier, as Hanbei eats, he shares some of the food with Suzu's son. Suzu explains that her husband was taken by war and if war starts again, she will lose Shoukichi and one day her child as well. Hanbei then stands up and thanks her for the food. Approaching the brigands, Hanbei states its been a long time since he had a reason to draw his blade and wonders if the brigands can kill him. The man laugh, thinking he is senile as his sword is broken. Two of the men attack Hanbei, but he quickly kills them. One of the remaining men then decides to take Hanbei alone. As the man is tall and uses overhead stance, Hanbei knows that he can't block or dodge, so he decides to deflect. The man is surprised that Hanbei deflected his first strike, but he follows with another strike right away, cutting down Hanbei. As Hanbei falls to the ground, he recalls Suzu asking him of his name. Hanbei explains that he left his name behind long ago, but down the line he became known as Hanbei the Undying. Hanbei then stands up.
